title: A Result Has to Explain Why It Belongs
description: On 12 April 2026 relationships, time, an APQC tree, local classification, unified search, and chunk embeddings land in the same model so a hit can carry its context.
body:
Finding a document is not the same as knowing what it is for. A flat pile of similar paragraphs will answer a question fluently and still be unable to say who it belongs to, when it was valid, or what it depends on. That is search as atmosphere. It is not a knowledge model.

On 12 April 2026 I bring entity relationships, enterprise types, temporal validity, an APQC folder tree, local classification, unified search routing, and chunk-level semantic search into the same day’s work. The question is no longer only whether VALESKA can find material. It is whether a result can carry enough context to explain what it represents.

Links, time, and a shared vocabulary

A document may describe a process, support a project, refer to a system, and remain true only for a period. Treating those as loose tags makes retrieval easy to start and hard to trust. Relationships are explicit: uses, depends on, supersedes, contradicts, collaborates with. Enterprise types now include the ordinary working kinds — system, service, team, person, project, process, decision, document, category. Time is recorded on the entity registry as valid-from, valid-until, and superseded-by. That is not yet temporal decay on retrieval. It is a place to keep the history of a description without pretending last year’s name is still current.

The APQC tree is built as Alfresco folders — forty-seven created in the recorded run, none skipped. Local classification can now call a local LM Studio model as well as the older path-and-name rules. A second method is not automatically a better method. It is a reviewable alternative. Unified search can merge VALESKA and Alfresco hits and degrade if one side is down. Chunking splits a long file into overlapping windows and embeds those windows at 384 dimensions, with overlapping defaults of a thousand tokens and two hundred of stride. Neither unified search nor chunks are a substitute for the source record, the classification, the relationship, and the period.

Relatedness extractors can propose similar, references, and entity links into file relationships. Those proposals are records. They are not a proof that two documents contradict each other. A later contradiction service is not in this day’s work and should not be smuggled in by a confident sentence. A relationship you can open and disagree with is already more useful than a similarity score with no name.

What this is not

There is no contradiction service. There is no claim that Alfresco is the permission gate. There is no evaluation harness proving recall improved. A fluent passage from a chunk is still a passage. The platform has to retain the path that lets a later reader ask whether the relationship, the process code, or the retrieved window was the right one.

The next test

The next step is a real question: from a search hit to the source, through the relationship and the process code, with the period still visible. The test is not an impressive summary. It is whether the structure helps someone investigate without losing the basis for the answer.

Historical basis: VALESKA commits 6076ed0, 2b9ac0e, 4f2bf81, and d94ae1b, April 12, 2026. The APQC tree count (47 created) is from the contemporaneous dispatch record of that run.

data.coverAlt: A globe of related entities — buildings, books, hours, ships — joined by gold lines between two landscapes: a model that can explain why a result belongs.
